params.hypothesis: ROOT (supported). Output 0 = sigmoid(z), z = 1.399 + 48 direct input terms + 12 hidden readouts (9 child annotations); 52 of the 107 one-hot/standardized inputs are unconnected and listed here as zero-effect entries. Class 1 is the 76% majority (presumably <=50K), so negative weights push toward high income. The model is essentially a sparse logistic regression with one consequential nonlinearity. Direct edges carry logit SD 3.37 of 3.85 (mean-ablating them drops train AUC 0.910->0.518); all hidden readouts together carry SD 1.32 and mean-ablating every hidden unit costs only acc 0.856->0.838, AUC 0.910->0.895. The only nonlinearity that matters is age_late_career_hinge (4647): keeping it alone recovers acc 0.850 / AUC 0.904. It turns the direct age slope (-0.88) into a U-shaped age effect with its minimum at age z~0.8. The other children are lookups or affine relays: capital_gain_affine_relay steepens the capital-gain slope to -2.54/SD; relationship1_indicator (-1.03 for relationship:1), occupation0_country0_gate (+0.92 for occupation:0 unless native-country:0), occupation8_relays (+0.45) and occupation1_relays (+0.37) are category offsets; country32_affine_relay and the native-country:4 part of the age hinge memorise rare countries; occupation6_relationship1_gate is near-inert (<=0.10 logit); dead_relationship_chain (613->2245->8678->170) and node 2114 are identically 0 on every valid input. Children combine ADDITIVELY in the logit (each child exit has one readout edge into node 0; no child feeds another). Largest exact logit-space attributions (mean |phi|, full train): relationship:0 0.82, education-num 0.72, marital-status:2 0.70, capital-gain 0.68, age 0.51, relationship:1 0.39, relationship:5 0.24, sex 0.23, occupation:8 0.21, hours-per-week 0.18.
